edbDesc: A pressure surge or wave resulting when a fluid in motion is forced to stop or change direction suddenly (Momentum Change). Water hammer commonly occurs when a valve is closed suddenly at an end of a pipeline system, and a pressure wave propagates in the pipe.
title: Water hammer
description: Shut a tap suddenly on fast-flowing water and the pipes bang, because the moving water slams to a stop and sends a pressure spike racing back through the pipe. Nikolai Zhukovsky worked out its size in 1898 after Moscow's water mains kept bursting. The hydraulic ram pump harnesses those bangs to lift water uphill with no motor at all.
effect: a moving liquid stopped suddenly sends a sharp pressure spike along its pipe
strength: Stopping water moving at 1 metre per second all at once raises the pressure by about 14 atmospheres.
pickWhy: Specific named effect with a clear job (ram pumps); titled Water hammer, its common name.
